paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. Paul tells Timothy to be strong, and then he says where the strength comes from: "the grace that is in Christ Jesus" (2 Timothy 2:1). Not your own hustle, friend. Not your grit, not your good mornings, not your perfect streak of getting it right. I've tried running on my own power, and that's how I ended up out of juice and in the back of a drawer.

Then Paul gives three pictures: a soldier, a competitor and a farmer (2 Timothy 2:3-6). The soldier lives to please the one who enlisted him, the competitor plays by the rules, and the farmer works hard. Every one of them says the same thing: following Jesus is a real commitment, and it can cost you something. Paul says it plainly, and he lives it, because he's chained like a criminal for the gospel, "But the word of God cannot be chained!" (2 Timothy 2:9). I think that's the kind of hope that gets a person through a hard week.

And look at what holds the whole thing up. Paul says, "if we are faithless, He remains faithful, for He cannot deny Himself" (2 Timothy 2:13). He's also honest that there's a warning in that saying: "if we deny Him, He will also deny us" (2 Timothy 2:12). So take Christ seriously, baker. But when you stumble, and you will, your hope doesn't rest on how well you held on to Him. It rests on how faithfully He holds on to you.
